ADHD is one of the most misunderstood neurodevelopmental conditions. Unfortunately, myths and misconceptions can delay diagnosis, increase stigma, and prevent individuals from getting the support they need.

🚩 Early Signs of Autism: What Parents Should Know

Recognizing early developmental differences can help children access support and interventions sooner.

Common early signs may include:
✓ Limited eye contact
✓ Delayed speech or language development
✓ Not responding consistently to their name
✓ Repetitive movements or behaviors
✓ Difficulty engaging in social interactions

Square Breathing (Box Breathing): A Simple Technique for Panic Attacks

When anxiety or panic starts to rise, square breathing can help slow your breathing and calm your body’s stress response.

⬜ Step 1: Breathe in through your nose for 4 seconds
⬜ Step 2: Hold your breath for 4 seconds
⬜ Step 3: Breathe out slowly through your mouth for 4 seconds
⬜ Step 4: Hold your breath again for 4 seconds

Repeat this cycle for 1–3 minutes or until you feel calmer.

Why it helps:
During a panic attack, breathing often becomes rapid and shallow. Square breathing encourages slow, controlled breaths, which can reduce physical symptoms such as a racing heart, dizziness, and feelings of panic.

Remember: Panic attacks are uncomfortable but not dangerous. Controlled breathing can help your body regain a sense of balance and control.

I want to share my experience with Dr. Amitabh Ghosh, a psychotherapist who works deeply with trauma, especially childhood trauma, using modalities like psychodrama and EMDR.

When I first started therapy with him, I was in an extremely fragile mental state. I was experiencing schizophrenic-like attacks and hallucinations. My anxiety was so severe that I was scared to step out of my house, scared to take a lift, scared to sit in a car, metro, or any moving vehicle. I was terrified of water bodies, small spaces, and even fears that are hard to explain or imagine. My life felt completely restricted by fear.

We started therapy from that point. It took me some time to understand his working style, but what stood out the most is that he never forces therapy on you. He truly believes that healing happens when you choose it. He creates a space where you arrive at therapy by yourself, in your own readiness, and that philosophy changed everything for me.

Initially, psychodrama was difficult for me because I was very much in my mind, trying to control and intellectualize everything. But as we continued, I slowly built trust, learned to let go, and switched off my analytical mind. That’s when the real transformation began.

What makes Dr. Ghosh different is his deep love and respect for his discipline. I’ve seen him constantly reading, learning, and researching—even between sessions. His commitment to understanding the human mind and trauma at the root level is rare. He doesn’t work on surface symptoms; he always goes to the root cause, and that’s where real healing happens.

My healing journey with him has been incredibly smooth and profound. Today, I can honestly say I’ve reached around 80% of my healing journey, and my entire life has changed. I have worked with multiple therapists before, but he was the last therapist I gave myself a chance with—and it worked in the most magical, almost miraculous way.

If you are looking for help for yourself or a loved one, I highly recommend Dr. Amitabh Ghosh. This is the kind of therapist you should give a genuine try. For me, he has been the best therapeutic guide I’ve ever met.

And if you ever come across this review, I truly believe it’s not a coincidence. Maybe God led you here. Please don’t ignore it—give this a chance.

10/10 recommended.
Love and peace.

🧠 PTSD: Trauma Doesn’t Have to Define Your Future

A frightening accident, physical assault, abuse, war, natural disaster, or the sudden loss of a loved one can leave emotional scars that continue long after the event is over.

Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD) is a genuine medical condition—not a sign of weakness. It affects how the brain processes fear, memory, and emotions, and it can interfere with work, relationships, sleep, and daily life.

⚠️ Common Symptoms
• Recurrent flashbacks or nightmares
• Avoiding reminders of the trauma
• Feeling emotionally numb or detached
• Irritability or anger outbursts
• Hypervigilance (always “on guard”)
• Poor sleep and concentration
• Feelings of guilt, shame, or hopelessness

💚 The Good News? PTSD is Treatable.

Evidence-based treatments such as:
✅ Trauma-focused Cognitive Behaviour Therapy (CBT)
✅ EMDR (Eye Movement Desensitization & Reprocessing)
✅ Appropriate medications (when needed)
✅ Stress management and lifestyle changes
can significantly improve recovery and quality of life.
🌱 Early treatment often leads to better outcomes.

🧠 Do You Find Yourself Repeatedly Pulling Your Hair? It Could Be Trichotillomania.

Hair pulling is not simply a "bad habit." For many people, it is a treatable mental health condition called Trichotillomania (Hair Pulling Disorder).

People with trichotillomania often experience:
✔ Repeated pulling of scalp hair, eyebrows, eyelashes, or beard hair
✔ Difficulty controlling the urge despite wanting to stop
✔ Temporary relief after pulling
✔ Visible hair thinning or bald patches
✔ Feelings of embarrassment, guilt, or low confidence

This condition can affect children, teenagers, and adults. Stress, anxiety, boredom, perfectionism, or emotional distress may worsen symptoms.

The good news is that effective treatments are available. Evidence-based approaches such as Habit Reversal Training (HRT), Cognitive Behaviour Therapy (CBT), and appropriate medications when needed can significantly reduce hair-pulling urges and improve quality of life.

Early treatment can prevent progression and help restore confidence.
